event_name: Stephen Wilson Jr at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb:
Stephen Wilson Jr closes out the week at the Roxy on Wednesday night. He's a country-rooted singer-songwriter with a voice that sits somewhere between classic Nashville and something more soulful, the kind of artist who tends to build a devoted following quietly before the broader world catches up.

Mid-week show at a great venue, and if you haven't caught him live yet, this is a good time to get in front of it. Tickets are available on the Battery's site.
scoring_notes: Stephen Wilson Jr is a rising artist but not yet a major draw, which limits uniqueness. Country and Americana music has real appeal in the Atlanta suburbs. Wednesday night timing is a drawback for a newsletter serving busy professionals and families. Included for variety but ranks lowest of the eight.

event_name: Vinings Jubilee Annual Christmas Tree Lighting
blurb:
It's the first night of the issue window and Vinings Jubilee is kicking it off right. The annual tree lighting around the Clocktower is one of those events that actually feels like a neighborhood moment, not just a thing to scroll past. Live performances from Whitefield Jazz Academy, Piccadilly Puppets, the Tinseltown Carolers, and more. Santa is there. Train rides are there. Face painting and ornament making are there.

After the lighting, pop into one of the shops or restaurants along the row and make a full evening of it. Free admission, easy parking, and genuinely festive. If you're looking for something to do on a Thursday night that gets the season started on the right foot, this is a solid pick.
scoring_notes: Vinings is close to the Perimeter coverage area and the event draws a mixed crowd of families and adults. The Thursday timing is a slight drawback but the opening-night-of-the-week positioning gives it relevance as an issue anchor event. Free admission is a neutral factor for this income level.

event_name: Roswell Dance Starz Presents: "The Roswell City Spectacular"
blurb:
Think Radio City Rockettes energy but closer to home and built by a local dance company that's clearly putting everything into it. The Roswell City Spectacular is a high-production holiday dance show with precision choreography, big costumes, and festive numbers designed to feel genuinely spectacular rather than just serviceable.

It's billed as a brand-new holiday tradition, which means this is the ground floor. If it's as good as the production suggests, people are going to be talking about it next year as the thing they wish they'd gone to. Good reason to go now. Check roswell365.com for show times and tickets.
scoring_notes: The 'brand new tradition' angle gives this more uniqueness than a standard Nutcracker. Roswell is a reasonable drive for Perimeter readers. Family-friendly with adult appeal. Missing time details in the source data is a minor issue but not disqualifying.

blurb:
Five private homes in Marietta's Church-Cherokee neighborhood, decked out for the holidays and open to the public for one day. That's the Marietta Pilgrimage Home Tour, and it's exactly as charming as it sounds. You're walking through real homes, not staged sets, each one decorated differently and with actual character. Historic churches and buildings are part of the route too.

Online tickets are $40 and sales close Wednesday, December 3rd at 4pm, so if you want the discount, today is the day to move on it. The proceeds benefit Cobb Landmarks and Historical Society, which means your ticket does something beyond getting you through the door. Worth the drive out to Marietta for anyone who's into design, history, or just a beautiful December morning.
scoring_notes: Annual event but only happens once a year with a specific home lineup, which keeps the uniqueness score respectable. Strong fit for the educated, design-aware Perimeter professional demographic, particularly empty nesters and adult couples. The advance ticket deadline creates genuine urgency in the newsletter.

blurb:
If you know Sabaton, you already know you need to be there. If you don't, here's the short version: they're a Swedish heavy metal band that writes exclusively about military history, real battles, real soldiers, real moments. It sounds niche until you're standing in a room full of people singing along to a song about the Battle of the Bulge and you realize this band has built something genuinely unlike anything else in rock music.

Tuesday night at the Roxy. This is not the kind of band that swings through Atlanta every few months. When they come, you go. Grab tickets at the Battery's site before the floor fills up.
scoring_notes: Sabaton is a niche pick for a general local newsletter, but the Perimeter audience skews toward educated professionals who appreciate novelty and unique experiences. High uniqueness score because they're a rare touring act. Scores docked on demographic and audience match because heavy metal is a narrower taste segment.

blurb:
Right in the heart of Dunwoody, Mitzvah House is turning Ashford Lane into the Menorah Chocolate Factory for a sweet Chanukah morning. It's free, it's family-friendly, and it's exactly the kind of neighborhood thing that you stumble onto once and then tell people about for years.

Spots are limited and RSVP is required, so if this sounds like your Sunday morning, grab your spot before they're gone. It's a fun, low-pressure way to get the kids into the holiday spirit without fighting traffic or spending a dime.
scoring_notes: Dunwoody and the broader Perimeter area have a significant Jewish population, making this a strong community fit. The free price point isn't the draw here, the neighborhood specificity and limited availability are. Good young families pick for Sunday morning.

event_name: The Nutcracker presented by Roswell Dance Theatre
date: Friday, December 4 & Saturday, December 5 & Sunday, December 6
time: Friday 7:00 PM | Saturday 2:00 PM & 7:00 PM | Sunday 2:00 PM
venue: Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center, Sandy Springs
blurb:
The Nutcracker at Byers Theatre is basically a Perimeter-area December rite of passage at this point, and Roswell Dance Theatre puts on a production that earns that reputation every year. We're talking world-class professional dancers sharing the stage with company students, a full cast, spectacular sets, and the kind of choreography that makes the Kingdom of Sweets feel genuinely magical.

This weekend has three shows left in the run, including a Saturday Meet and Greet performance where kids can get photos and autographs with the characters after the curtain. If you've got little ones who are into dance, or honestly just anyone who wants a proper holiday night out, this is a legitimately beautiful production a few miles from home.

Tickets are on sale now at RoswellNutcracker.com. The run ends Sunday, so don't sit on this one.
scoring_notes: Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center is basically in the Perimeter audience's backyard. Strong appeal across both young families and empty nesters. The Nutcracker is a recurring annual event, which docks uniqueness a point, but the limited remaining performances in the window create real urgency.

event_name: BLOOPER's Holiday Clubhouse Experience at Truist Park
blurb:
This one is genuinely hard to replicate. BLOOPER's Holiday Clubhouse Experience gets you and up to five guests behind the scenes at Truist Park during the off-season, which means the clubhouse, the batting cages, the dugout, and if the weather cooperates, actual catch on the field. That's not a thing you can just do on a random Tuesday.

Throw BLOOPER Claus into the mix, a festive digital photo op, and a chance to snap pics with the 2026 NL East Pennant, and you've got a holiday memory that beats anything you'd find at a mall. The 20% off at the Braves Clubhouse Store is a nice bonus if you've still got gifts to knock out.

If you've got kids who bleed Braves blue, or a spouse who does, this is the move. Book it before it fills up.
scoring_notes: Perimeter skews toward young families and young professionals with solid household income, both of whom index heavily toward Atlanta sports fandom. The behind-the-scenes access is genuinely rare and can't be replicated at other holiday events. Strong family fit without being exclusively kid-focused.

venue: Park Bench at The Battery ATL, Atlanta
blurb:
No cover, Saturday night, three hours of crowd-driven live music at The Battery. Park Bench's Dueling Pianos show is the kind of thing that works for a bachelorette party, a friend group that just wants to do something, or two people who skipped their usual Saturday routine and wanted to feel spontaneous.

The format is simple: two pianists, audience requests, and a room that gets louder as the night goes on. It's not a seated, quiet experience. It's interactive and a little unpredictable, which is exactly what makes it fun. No cover means your only financial commitment is whatever you order from the bar, so the risk of showing up and deciding it's not your scene is basically zero.

Tables fill up, though. If you want a guaranteed seat, reserve one ahead of time. Otherwise, get there before 8:30 and find a spot before the room figures out what it is.
scoring_notes: Dueling Pianos is a recurring event at Park Bench, which keeps uniqueness lower. But the no-cover format and Saturday night timing make it very accessible and low-risk. Works well for the younger end of the East Cobb demographic and established families looking for a night out without the kids. The Battery location is familiar to East Cobb residents. Slightly lower scores because it's not a one-time event and skews younger than the core audience.

blurb:
If the typical holiday show doesn't quite do it for you, this one has a different energy. The Alley Stage is hosting A Very Marietta Christmas Cabaret on Wednesday, December 9, and it's exactly what it sounds like: local talent, a mix of Christmas classics and jazzy holiday standards, some humor, and a room that feels nothing like a formal theater.

Cabaret format means smaller venue, tables instead of rows, and performers who are actually playing to you rather than projecting to a thousand-seat house. The show pulls in some of the stronger voices on the local theater scene and the repertoire reportedly includes a few surprises alongside the standards. It's 18+, so this is a grown-up night out, and a midweek one at that, which makes it feel a little more spontaneous and a little less scheduled.

If you've got a friend who loves live music but doesn't want to sit through a formal concert, this is the one to suggest.
scoring_notes: Cabaret format is more niche than a standard holiday concert, which is both a strength (uniqueness) and a slight risk (smaller potential audience). 18+ designation makes it adult-only, which fits the empty nester portion of this audience well. Wednesday night timing limits turnout potential but gives it a distinctive spontaneous feel. The Alley Stage is a small, intimate venue that appeals to arts-curious East Cobb residents.

blurb:
December is not exactly peak Beach Boys season, and that's kind of the point.

Sail On brings a full Beach Boys tribute experience to the Roswell Cultural Arts Center on Sunday afternoon, December 6, running from 4 to 6 PM. If you grew up on "Good Vibrations," "Wouldn't It Be Nice," or "California Girls," this is two hours of pure nostalgia at a venue close enough that you're home for dinner. The 42-year median age of East Cobb skews this crowd perfectly toward people who actually know these songs by heart, not people who Shazamed them on a playlist.

Sunday at 4 PM is a genuinely low-commitment ask. No babysitter drama, no late night, just a good afternoon out. Grab a friend who always has the oldies station on during road trips and go enjoy it.
scoring_notes: Beach Boys tribute skews toward the 40-55 demographic strongly, which aligns well with East Cobb's median age of 42. Roswell is close and accessible. Sunday afternoon timing is very low friction. The holiday-counter-programming angle (Beach Boys in December) is a mild but real differentiator. Not a one-of-a-kind event but tribute shows are specific enough to earn a moderate uniqueness score.

blurb:
A live orchestra playing holiday classics on a Saturday night, right in Marietta. That's the pitch, and it's a good one.

The Holiday Pops concert at the Marietta Performing Arts Center on December 5 runs from 7:30 to 9:30 PM and covers exactly what you'd want from a night like this: festive favorites, heartwarming standards, and the kind of full orchestral sound that a Spotify playlist genuinely cannot replicate. There are sing-along moments built into the show, which either sounds fun to you or it doesn't, but either way the music alone is worth showing up for.

This is a clean, easy Saturday night plan. Nice venue, close to home, and you're back before midnight. Grab dinner in Marietta Square first and you've got a full evening with almost no effort required.
scoring_notes: Live orchestral holiday concerts appeal strongly to the 40+ demographic with college-educated homeowners. Marietta PAC is close and familiar to East Cobb residents. Saturday evening timing is ideal. The sing-along element and festive tone make it accessible without being lowbrow. Works for couples, empty nesters, and established families. Slightly lower uniqueness because holiday pops concerts happen every year.

event_name: Roswell Dance Theatre presents The Nutcracker
date: Friday, December 4 and Saturday, December 5 and Sunday, December 6
venue: Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center, Sandy Springs
blurb:
If your family has a Nutcracker tradition, Roswell Dance Theatre has been one of the best versions of it in metro Atlanta for years. This weekend is your last chance to catch it, with performances Friday evening, Saturday afternoon and evening, and a Sunday matinee to close things out on December 6.

What sets RDT's production apart is the mix of professional dancers and local students on the same stage, all under a creative team that's been doing this for a long time. The sets are real, the choreography is real, and Clara's journey from the holiday party to the Kingdom of Sweets still lands the way it's supposed to. Saturday's 2 PM and Sunday's 2 PM performances also include Character Meet and Greet options, which younger kids in the crowd will not forget.

This is the final weekend of the run. If you've been meaning to go, this is it.
scoring_notes: The Nutcracker is a recurring annual production but this is the final weekend, which adds genuine urgency. East Cobb families with teens and younger kids are core Nutcracker audience. Sandy Springs is close enough that it's a realistic outing. RDT is a well-regarded local company. Works for established families and grandparents visiting for the holidays.

event_name: Pie and Whiskey Pairing at ASW Distillery
venue: ASW Distillery at The Battery ATL, Atlanta
blurb:
ASW Distillery and Pie Bar did the research so you don't have to, and the results are exactly what you'd hope for on a December Sunday afternoon.

This guided tasting pairs four of ASW's award-winning craft whiskeys with four fresh-baked mini pies: Bourbon Chocolate Pecan with Fiddler Soloist Bourbon, Tart Cherry Crumble with Duality Double Malt, Peppermint Chocolate Cream with Resurgens Rye, and Brown Sugar Chess with ASW's American Single Malt. Each pairing was developed through actual R&D, not guesswork, and the result is a 90-minute experience that covers a lot of ground in a very enjoyable way.

It's at The Battery, so you can make a full afternoon of it before or after. This is a great pick for empty nesters looking for something a little more interesting than the usual holiday wine night, or for anyone who wants to give the gift of actually doing something fun together.
scoring_notes: Pie and whiskey pairing is genuinely unusual and memorable. ASW is a well-regarded Atlanta distillery with a real following. The Battery location is familiar and accessible to East Cobb residents. Adult-only skew works well for the empty nester portion of this audience. $118K median income means ticket price is a non-issue. Slightly lower audience match because it's a drive to Atlanta and skips the family segment entirely.

event_name: Menorah Lighting at Avenue East Cobb
blurb:
This one is literally in your backyard. Avenue East Cobb is teaming up with Chabad of Cobb to celebrate the first night of Chanukah with a traditional menorah lighting ceremony on Sunday, December 6, starting at 5:30 PM.

Beyond the lighting itself, there will be family-friendly activities, Chanukah treats, and the event everyone's going to be talking about: the Gelt Drop. Cobb County Fire Department brings out a truck, raises the ladder to its highest point, and rains chocolate coins down on the crowd below. Kids love it. Adults love it. Honestly, it sounds fun for anyone with a pulse.

Free, close to home, and something a little different for a Sunday evening. Worth putting on the calendar.
scoring_notes: East Cobb has a significant Jewish population and Chabad of Cobb is active in the area. Avenue East Cobb is literally in the coverage zone. The Gelt Drop angle is genuinely fun and unusual, boosting uniqueness. Free event, so price is irrelevant. Works for families with teens and empty nesters alike. First night of Chanukah adds cultural significance and timeliness.

blurb:
Every year, a handful of Marietta's most beautiful private homes open their doors for the holidays, and every year, it sells out the conversation at dinner tables across East Cobb for weeks after.

The Marietta Pilgrimage Christmas Home Tour is back on Saturday, December 5, and this year's route takes you through five stunning homes in the Church-Cherokee Neighborhood, each decorated to the nines for the season. Beyond the homes themselves, the tour also winds through some of Marietta's historic churches and museums, so you're getting a full slice of what makes this city actually worth living near.

This is a Cobb Landmarks & Historical Society event, which means the proceeds go back into preserving the stuff that makes the area worth caring about. At $40 a ticket, it's a genuinely good afternoon out, and the kind of thing that gets better when you bring a friend or your spouse and make a day of it in downtown Marietta. One important note: online ticket sales close Wednesday, December 3 at 4 PM. If you're reading this and thinking "I'll grab them later," later is now.
scoring_notes: Annual event but only one day per year, which keeps the uniqueness score high. Historic home tours skew heavily toward 40+ homeowners with disposable income, which is exactly this audience. $40 is a non-issue at $118K median HHI. Works great for couples, empty nesters, and established families. The December 3 ticket deadline adds real urgency for a December 3 newsletter drop.
